role_and_message.evidence: The motivation remains pixel-level ZS3 versus decoupled class-agnostic grouping and segment-level zero-shot classification.

panel_and_object_coverage.evidence: Four full evidence images, original seen/unseen color legend, baseline method and decoupled method panels are retained.

labels_math_and_numbers.evidence: Original semantic labels including mistakes in predictions, seen wood/person/sea/water-other and unseen river/tree/frisbee remain exact, with all method block names preserved.

connections_and_direction.evidence: Both method entry arrows and baseline exit arrow are restored. Pixel embeddings and language model enter baseline classification; segment embeddings branch to grouping/classification, vision-language model enters classification and both outputs merge.

visual_encodings.evidence: Original category color legend and pixel-map colors match because the whole legend and all result maps are native source crops.

examples_and_data.evidence: All five protected blocks independently match source RGB pixels at native1x: photograph, human annotation, seen/unseen legend and both prediction maps.

unsupported_additions.evidence: Panel headings restate the original caption and introduction. Restored input/output arrows reproduce original topology rather than adding a new dependency.

complete_visible_content.evidence: All three complete panels and label-bearing evidence images are visible; method arrows no longer omit the source entry/exit relationships.

remaining_limitations: Exact original source regions are preserved at native or integer nearest scale; enlarged small labels retain original pixel detail. Fidelity audit does not independently validate scientific conclusions.
caption:
Figure 1. ZS3 aims to train a model merely on seen classes and
generalize it to classes that have not been seen in the training (un-
seen classes). Existing methods formulate it as a pixel-level zero-
shot classification problem (b), and use semantic features from a
language model to transfer the knowledge from seen classes to
unseen ones. In contrast, as in (c), we decouple ZS3 into two
sub-tasks: 1) A class-agnostic grouping and 2) A segment-level
zero-shot classification, which enables us to take full advantage of
the pre-trained vision-language model.
